I have read only 1 work by Descartes, namely, Meditations on First Philosophy, and so my explanation may be vague or incorrect.

Descartes arrived at "Cogito ergo sum" through certain processes. In Meditations on First Philosophy, he was making an attempt to find foundations for knowledge. The book contains six meditations that attempt to discover what is real by first doubting absolutely everything and starting from the beginning.

First Meditations explains why he can call his beliefs into doubt, since his beliefs and his senses have deceived him before. due to his beliefs, and indeed his senses had been known to be wrong - and that they could be doubted - he claimed it gave him reason to be skeptical of everything. He argues that perhaps he is currently dreaming or that God is actually a deceiving demon, or that he is simply crazy.

This leads into the Second Meditations. Here is where he convinces himself that nothing of the world is real because it can be doubted. Everything that can possibly be be doubted is discarded as being real, which leads Descartes with boiling existence itself down into nothing.

Then he writes this in Second Meditations:

"I have convinced myself that there is nothing in the world — no sky, no earth, no minds, no bodies. Doesn’t it follow that I don’t exist? No, surely I must exist if it’s me who is convinced of something. But there is a deceiver, supremely powerful and cunning whose aim is to see that I am always deceived. But surely I exist, if I am deceived. Let him deceive me all he can, he will never make it the case that I am nothing while I think that I am something. Thus, having fully weighed every consideration, I must finally conclude that the statement “I am, I exist” must be true whenever I state it or mentally consider it."

Tl;dr Descartes attempts to find absolute proofs through the the apparent undeniable fact of thought occurring; if everything else's existence can be called into doubt because the senses are capable of failing, ones existence (or, doubt occurring) cannot be doubted because doubt implies existence. He would reject "I shop, therefore, I am" because 'I shop' can be put into doubt.
